sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to the Medical 3D Dice and HD95 Boundary Divergence Studio. In this interactive lab, you can test how different tumor segmentation errors impact both bulk volumetric Dice and surface boundary distance. Notice that when you select the Dangerous Portal Vein Spike, the Dice score stays deceptive at 0.938 while HD95 explodes to 8.4 millimeters, rightfully triggering a clinical hazard warning!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Kaito, try toggling the Dangerous Portal Vein Spike scenario. Notice how the candidate contour penetrates right into the portal vein. Even though the bulk Dice score looks great at 0.938, the 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance spikes to 8.4 millimeters, halting automated surgical approval!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 1: A deep learning model segments a 60-cubic-centimeter pancreatic adenocarcinoma with a high Dice score of 0.948, but the 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance is 8.2 millimeters protruding directly into the Superior Mesenteric Artery. What is your engineering and surgical decision?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Let's analyze Checkpoint 1, Kaito. The model achieved a 0.948 Dice score, but an 8.2-millimeter boundary spike penetrates an adjacent major artery. Should the oncology board accept or reject this automated contour?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Spot on, Machine Learning Architect! Bulk Dice is a volumetric ratio that completely dilutes narrow boundary spikes. An 8.2-millimeter arterial infiltration represents less than 0.25 percent of the total tumor volume, so Dice remains deceptively high while creating a lethal surgical laceration risk. The contour must be rejected!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Not quite. Remember that Dice measures bulk volume overlap, not surface boundary distance. In a 60-cubic-centimeter tumor, an 8.2-millimeter vascular spike accounts for a tiny fraction of total voxels, leaving Dice high while creating a fatal arterial laceration risk during surgery. The contour must be rejected!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to the 7-DOF Oriented 3D Bounding Box and BEV IoU Studio. Experiment with the range and yaw sliders to see how heading error quickly collapses 3D IoU below the 0.70 threshold. You can also switch to the Legal Fuzzy Span tab to inspect exact matching versus token overlap in commercial contracts.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Kaito, try twisting the yaw heading slider to 15 degrees on the BEV canvas. Even with identical box centers and sizes, the 3D IoU immediately collapses below 0.70! And check out the Legal tab to see how fuzzy token overlap prevents unfair punctuation penalties.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 2: An autonomous vehicle perception stack has a 45-millisecond clock drift between camera frames and LiDAR sweeps. At highway closing speeds of 108 kilometers per hour, or 30 meters per second, an annotator labels an oncoming truck with a 15-degree yaw heading error. What is the spatial displacement, and what happens to the 3D IoU and trajectory tracker?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Let's work through Checkpoint 2, Kaito. At 30 meters per second, what physical distance does an obstacle travel in 45 milliseconds, and what does a 15-degree yaw mismatch do to the Bird's-Eye View 3D IoU?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Precisely right! Multiplying 30 meters per second by 0.045 seconds yields 1.35 meters of physical spatial displacement, tearing the LiDAR points away from camera pixels. Combined with a 15-degree yaw rotation, 3D IoU collapses below 0.70, triggering false trajectory predictions and phantom braking!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Not quite. At 108 kilometers per hour, closing velocity is 30 meters per second. In 45 milliseconds, the obstacle moves 1.35 meters, creating a massive multi-modal offset. Furthermore, a 15-degree yaw error collapses 3D IoU below 0.70, severely disrupting Kalman tracking filters.
